page.layout: One column of verse, set indented in lines, left of centre; below it at the right the catchword "Fraun-". No running head, page number or marginal notes on this page. Faint show-through from the other side is ignored.

main_text.p: Digné queratur sub Babylonii Duro peracta Pontificis jugo: Sive est Abaddon ille, multis Bellua seu capitata monstris, Sive huius est dorsum mulier premens, Circaea miscens pocula regibus, Juere cui servitum ab imis Quotquot erant, medii, supremi, Captiva turba, & mille quidem jugum Cervice portatura per amplius Annos. Peracto, o si, quod optem, Exierint mala saecla cursu Determinato coelitus, ut novi Feliciori sidere prodeant Menses, & opportuniore Auspicio repetantur orbes. Fato locustarum agminibus dati, Tantum malorum pertulit impio Sub saeculo Europaeus orbis, Mille humeros onerare vatum Quod posser[?] omnes & validos quidem. O si quis, olim ut Nabuchodonosor, Coelo coortus nunc & alter Exigat, o scelerata poenas

page.notes: The verse is one unbroken poem with no stanza breaks, so it is set as a single paragraph with line breaks kept. "Digné" carries the printed acute accent. "peracta" is printed with a ct ligature. "posser" is doubtful: it may be "posse" or "posset" and is marked [?]. Where the printed text has u as a consonant (Captiua, Siue, seruitum, Iuere, iugo), it is given as v or j. The final line ends with a hyphenated catchword "Fraun-" at the right, which is the start of the next page's first word.
